title: Dual Structure-guided Contrastive Network for Incomplete Multi-view Partial Multi-label Classification

problem.claim: Incomplete multi-view partial multi-label classification addresses incompleteness in both multi-view and multi-label settings.

gap.claim: Existing methods overlook relationships among instances and missing label distributions, limiting representation quality and label-correlation modeling.

contributions.claim: DSCN is a model for incomplete multi-view partial multi-label classification.
The model combines instance-level contrastive learning with multi-view attention-based fusion to produce consistent, discriminative, and robust consensus representations.
The model combines a multi-view shared classifier with label-level contrastive learning to use complementary views and missing label distributions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present DSCN as a novel model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five benchmark datasets reportedly show that DSCN achieves more than 13% accuracy compared with state-of-the-art approaches.
The authors report that the code and datasets are available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: The task combines incompleteness across multiple views and labels.
Prior methods underuse instance relationships and missing-label distributions.
DSCN addresses representation learning through instance structure and attention-based multi-view fusion.
A shared classifier and label-structure contrastive mechanism improve prediction using complementary views and missing-label information.
The authors report gains on five benchmark datasets and provide code and datasets.

source_observation.claim: Using both instance structures and label structures can address distinct information gaps in incomplete multi-view partial multi-label learning.

interpretation.claim: A dual-structure design may improve learning when view incompleteness and label incompleteness create complementary modeling needs.

application.claim: For related incomplete multi-view and multi-label tasks, consider separate structure-aware mechanisms for instance representations and label prediction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which component is responsible for the reported improvement or whether the approach generalizes beyond the evaluated benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation metric underlying the reported accuracy improvement.
The five benchmark datasets, baselines, experimental settings, and statistical details are unspecified.
The effects of individual DSCN components and the exact missingness assumptions are unspecified.
